text:
devin: quick heads-up — i'm about to land a terraform module split that separates network/credentials into two modules. want a quick compat + secret wiring sanity check before i merge. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/482

sam: thanks — main questions: 1) provider blocks (root vs module) 2) lockfile pin strategy 3) k8s secret path changes that could break the sync job. :eyes:

devin: good call. plan specifics:
- hoist provider declarations to root (we'll use explicit provider aliases for gke/mysql where needed)
- remove provider blocks from submodules (they'll accept providers from root)
- run terraform providers lockfile regen as part of the PR pipeline (linux_amd64, linux_arm64)
- add a var secret_namespace + secret_path in creds module with defaults to current values so no immediate break

sam: sound reasonable. will you also add a migration note for any state moves? last time we had a tiny surprise with a resource reassign.

devin: yes — i'll run tf state mv for the few resources that move into the new module namespace and include the exact commands in the PR description. example commands in PR:```bash
# move the service account into the creds module state path
terraform state mv module.old_creds.google_service_account.main module.creds.google_service_account.main
```

jamie: for the k8s side, the secret-sync job reads annotations annotated-secret-path. if the new module changes annotation keys we need a migration or the job will no-op and cause secrets not to sync. can you confirm the annotation stays as-is?

devin: i'll keep the annotation key the same (annotations["redwood.com/secret-path"]) and expose secret_path var only so infra-as-code teams can customize. default equals old path. i'll also add a short smoke test in the PR that applies the k8s manifest to staging and asserts the sync job picks up the secret.

prash: small note — when you regenerate the lockfile, add the providers with pinned versions in a comment block in the PR so we can eyeball upgrades. also please run plan with the same TF version the infra CI uses (1.6.9) to avoid drift noise.

infra-bot: build/ci for PR #482: plan passed ✓ (modules changed: network, creds)

sam: ok lgtm pending your state mv commands and a short blurb about rollback steps. thanks for handling the aliasing — that should keep provider duplication out of the graph. :thumbsup:

devin: thanks — i'll push the followups (state mv snippet, lockfile regen note, and staging smoke test) in the next commit. ping @sam @jamie for final review once done. :shipit:
